results.observation: Ed25519 signs the SHA-512 digest of canonical JSON bytes. Modifying even 1 bit in the payload alters the hash digest entirely (avalanche effect). Modifying 1 bit of the signature breaks the equation [S]B = R + [H(R, A, M)]A, resulting in immediate rejection.

results.title: Sender Impersonation Attempt

results.observation: Digital signatures authenticate messages relative to a specific public key, NOT a real identity. Without out-of-band key authentication (SHA-256 fingerprint, PKI CA, or Key Transparency), an attacker substituting a public key in an untrusted directory successfully deceives the verifier.

results.title: Public-Key Substitution Attack & Defense

results.observation: Digital signatures provide integrity and authenticity, but zero confidentiality. In Part A, any wire interceptor reads the secret in plaintext. In Part B, Encrypt-then-Sign with AES-256-GCM ensures the payload is ciphertext on the wire while Ed25519 authenticates the entire envelope.

results.observation: Because an authentic digital signature remains mathematically valid indefinitely, passive attackers can replay recorded packets unless stateful defenses are present. Binding a monotonically increasing counter and timestamp inside the signed envelope blocks duplicate submission, while preventing the attacker from altering the counter.
